option_a: Serif

question: A headline is set in a bold slab typeface and the body copy in a light sans serif. This is an example of:
option_a: Type pairing with deliberate contrast

question: A poster uses four different decorative typefaces. The most likely result is:
option_a: The design reads as messy and the hierarchy weakens

question: For a long block of fine print at a small size, the most appropriate typeface choice is:
option_a: A clean, highly legible typeface

question: The single biggest hierarchy problem in this poster is:
option_a: There is no clear focal point because the levels are nearly the same size
option_b: The canvas dimensions are incorrect for a poster
option_c: The poster uses too few total colors
option_d: The photograph is raster rather than vector

option_a: Increase the contrast between the text and its background

question: To establish a clear reading order the designer should first:
option_a: Create a real size jump between the headline, the details, and the fine print
option_b: Center every element on the page
option_c: Set every line of text in bold

question: Visual hierarchy is best defined as:
option_a: The order in which a viewer notices elements
option_b: The number of layers in a design file
option_c: The ratio of the canvas width to its height

question: Visual weight is determined mainly by:
option_a: Size, color, and contrast

question: A designer squints at a poster and two elements remain equally readable. This indicates that:
option_a: The focal point is not clearly established
option_d: The file resolution is too low

question: Generous whitespace around a headline primarily:
option_a: Increases the prominence of the headline
option_d: Adds visual weight to the fine print

question: Placing the date, time, and location close together and away from the fine print applies the principle of:
option_a: Proximity

question: Aligning elements to shared edges primarily:
option_a: Creates an organized structure that guides the eye
option_b: Increases the saturation of the colors

question: Applying one bright accent color to a single element on an otherwise muted poster will most likely:
option_a: Draw the eye to that element first
option_b: Flatten the hierarchy of the page
option_c: Cause the poster to print darker overall

question: A poster uses five highly saturated competing colors. The most likely effect on hierarchy is that it:
option_a: Weakens, because no single element dominates
option_b: Strengthens, because more colors add contrast
option_c: Stays the same, since color does not affect hierarchy
option_d: Changes only in print, not on screen

question: A poster for a school wellness and nature club would most conventionally use:
option_a: Greens and earth tones

question: A designer needs a poster to communicate urgency about a closing deadline. The most conventional color choice is:
option_a: Red

question: Adding black to a hue produces a:
option_a: Shade

question: Colors positioned opposite one another on the color wheel are:
option_a: Complementary

question: A monochromatic color scheme is most likely to produce:
option_a: A unified look where contrast comes from value

question: A designer selects a vivid neon green on screen for a poster that will be commercially printed. The most likely outcome is that the printed color:
option_a: Appears duller than it did on screen
option_b: Appears brighter than it did on screen

question: The correct color mode for a file destined for a commercial ink printer is:
option_a: CMYK

question: A logo must be enlarged to banner size with no loss of quality. The appropriate format is:
option_a: A vector file

question: An image constructed from pixels is described as:
option_a: Raster

question: A designer needs one file for commercial printing and one to place on a web page. The appropriate pair is:
option_a: A PDF for print and a PNG or JPG for the web
option_c: The editable project file for both purposes
option_d: A RAW file for print and a PDF for the web

question: Delivering only the editable project file instead of an export is a problem because it:
option_a: Is not a finished file the recipient can open
option_d: Removes the hierarchy from the design

question: A transparent background is preserved by exporting as a:
option_a: PNG

question: Setting an entire paragraph of fine print in all capital letters most likely:
option_a: Reduces readability
option_c: Increases contrast with the headline only

question: Font weight refers to:
option_a: How bold or thin the strokes of a typeface are
option_b: The point size of the text
option_d: The width of the text column

question: A raster photograph placed at 300 percent of its native size on a printed poster will most likely:
option_a: Appear soft or pixelated in print
